Constraint Handling Rules (CHR) is a high-level programming language that incorporates constraints and reflective features. It's a multi-pass constraint logic programming language that allows for declarative specification of problems and solutions. In this study, we investigate the computational power of CHR with a finite number of atoms in a specific "head" and a single predicate, referred to as the "head predicate." Our research reveals that the expressive power of CHR is determined by the number of atoms in the head and the head predicate, and we establish that CHR with a finite number of atoms in the head and a single predicate can simulate any Turing machine. Furthermore, we analyze the computational complexity of CHR with a finite number of atoms in the head and a single predicate, and we establish that CHR with a finite number of atoms in the head and a single predicate can simulate any Turing machine.

We have analyzed the galaxy spin direction dipole in the SDSS, 2MRS, and LAMOST surveys, as well as in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) data at different redshifts. Our results show that the direction of the galaxy spin dipole remains consistent across various surveys and redshifts, despite the differences in galaxy sample selection. This consistency suggests that the galaxy spin dipole is a stable feature in the galaxy distribution, rather than a redshift-dependent effect.

Recent advancements in few-shot learning have been driven by the development of meta-learning methods, which can be trained on small datasets and generalize effectively to new tasks. However, current approaches often rely on unrealistic assumptions, such as perfectly sampled data and noise-free labels. To address these limitations, we introduce the Eigen-Reptile method, a novel approach that leverages the Eigen-Reptile optimizer to learn a meta-model. By combining this optimizer with a novel sampling strategy and label denoising technique, we can learn a meta-model that generalizes well even in the presence of noisy labels. Our experiments on various benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming current state-of-the-art methods.

A novel approach to predicting cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease has been developed by leveraging a large dataset of electronic health records. By analyzing longitudinal data from the ADNI study, researchers can forecast the time until a significant decline in Mini-Mental State Examination scores, which is a key indicator of disease progression. The proposed method, which involves a two-stage process, utilizes a semi-parametric model to identify patterns in the data and a machine learning algorithm to make predictions. The results show that this approach outperforms traditional methods, including a Cox proportional hazards model, and provides more accurate predictions. The method also offers insights into the factors that contribute to disease progression, which can inform treatment decisions.

This paper examines the current state of AI ethics research, with a focus on ethical considerations for AI systems. A comprehensive literature review is conducted to identify key areas of study, including the development of a framework to organize the findings. The analysis reveals a notable absence of guidelines for conducting ethical analyses in AI and highlights the need for established best practices in this regard. The study also identifies a significant gap in research on fairness and justice in AI systems, underscoring the importance of these considerations. Ultimately, the research identifies future directions for the field of AI ethics and recommends potential avenues for further exploration.

We investigate the decidability of containment and equivalence between finite languages of infinite words, a problem that has been a long-standing concern in theoretical computer science. Our research focuses on the properties of various classes of languages that can be defined using specific operators and shows that certain combinations of these operators lead to the only fully definable language families that satisfy specific criteria. By examining the properties of these classes, we are able to determine the exact relationship between the classes of languages that can be defined using different combinations of these operators. Our findings have significant implications for the study of containment and equivalence between finite collections of words, a problem that has been a long-standing concern in theoretical computer science.

This paper introduces a novel hybrid channel estimation approach that combines deep neural network (DNN) and super-resolution (SR) techniques. The proposed method utilizes a DNN to predict channel impulse responses from received signals, and then feeds these predictions into an SR module for more precise channel modeling. The SR module refines the predicted CIRs to achieve accurate channel estimation. The approach is tested on various 5G NR scenarios, including both single-cell and multi-cell environments. The results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances channel prediction accuracy, with a 2.5-fold improvement in mean square error compared to traditional methods.

Recent unusual data on the CKM matrix elements, Vud and Vus, have significant implications for our understanding of physics beyond the Standard Model. These anomalies can be resolved if the Standard Model is extended with a new particle, such as a Zprime boson, which interacts with leptons. We investigate the potential of future electron-positron colliders, such as the FCC-ee, to detect this new Zprime boson, which would decay into a muon and neutrino. Our analysis shows that the FCC-ee can cover a substantial portion of the viable parameter space of the Zprime model, which is currently constrained by the Belle II experiment.

This research introduces a novel network architecture for the semantic segmentation of images. The proposed network incorporates a dual convolution approach, where dilated kernels are employed in the initial convolution layers to enhance its receptive field and enable the extraction of low-level image details. Subsequently, an atrous spatial pyramid pooling layer is integrated to capture both local and global image characteristics. The output is then fed into a fully convolutional network, enabling the generation of dense, pixel-level predictions. The proposed network's efficacy is demonstrated through its application to the CamVid dataset, yielding superior results compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

We introduce a novel approach to achieve data privacy, where each data view is modified to conceal its individual attributes while preserving the common aspects. This separation of private and shared information is achieved through a process called factorization, which organizes the data into a joint and individual factor space. By applying a probabilistic method, the data is transformed into a factorized representation that incorporates both shared and private factors. This factorized data is then represented as a combination of a publicly accessible summary and a differential privacy-ensuring noise vector. This factorized representation enables the creation of a privacy-preserving data release that balances utility and privacy. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of this approach in creating useful data releases that meet privacy requirements.

A comprehensive study of 19,000 galaxies at a specific wavelength has been conducted, focusing on the relationship between dust heating, radio signals, and galaxy structure. The analysis, based on the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, reveals a correlation between radio activity, morphology, and a specific type of dust heating, suggesting that the heating of dust is closely tied to the processes that create radio signals. The study also finds that the heating of dust is more widespread in galaxies with high levels of radio activity and a specific spiral structure, indicating a complex interplay between these phenomena. The results suggest that the heating of dust is not solely the result of a specific type of starburst, but rather is influenced by a variety of factors, including radio activity and a specific type of galaxy.

Recent studies have shown that large language models can perform tasks similar to humans in moral reasoning, but they lack an understanding of the underlying reasoning. To address this, we developed MORALCOT, a novel prompting strategy that utilizes multiple prompts to teach large language models to recognize and replicate the key components of human moral reasoning. Our results demonstrate that MORALCOT significantly enhances a model's ability to comprehend and replicate human moral reasoning, outperforming a baseline model in a human evaluation study.
A valuation ring with a finite residue field characteristic of $p$ can be represented as the direct limit of $p$-ary Henselian domains.

This book offers a detailed examination of two-dimensional Dirac equation solutions, including an analysis of the relativistic and semi-relativistic Coulomb problems. It also explores the implications of Dirac-like equations in quantum mechanics, particularly in relation to the hydrogen atom. The discussion is further extended to encompass two-dimensional Dirac equation systems with external fields, such as electric, magnetic, and mixed fields, as well as time-dependent external fields. The book also covers the generalized Coulomb spherically symmetric Dirac equation and the Dirac equation in anti-wave and anti-kink wave backgrounds. The work is significant in the context of Dirac-like equations, offering new insights into the properties of two-dimensional Dirac equation solutions.

This paper introduces a novel Model Predictive Control (MPC) approach to enhance cooperative driving in autonomous vehicles. By leveraging the MPC controller's ability to optimize performance, the system can better navigate complex scenarios. To achieve this, the MPC controller must balance the needs of all road users while adhering to safety standards. In this research, the MPC controller is trained on a dataset of safe driving behaviors, which is then applied to real-world situations. To validate the system's effectiveness, the paper presents case studies demonstrating its ability to resolve road user conflicts and improve traffic flow.

The widespread use of social media has led to a situation where online content is often shared without being fact-checked, resulting in the dissemination of false information. This can be attributed to the way social media platforms operate, as they often prioritize quantity over quality, amplifying the reach of content regardless of its credibility. As a result, users are left with an overwhelming amount of information, making it challenging to distinguish between accurate and inaccurate content. This study aims to address this issue by developing a novel approach to detect misinformation on social media platforms. By analyzing the interactions between users and their social connections, our method identifies potential misinformation based on the patterns of engagement surrounding a given post. This approach has been tested on real-world data from Twitter, where we compared our method to existing solutions and found that it outperforms them in terms of accuracy.

This paper introduces $\pi$-ROAD, a framework that enables a robotic system to safely navigate road accidents and facilitate human interaction. By integrating a model-based approach with reinforcement learning, $\pi$-ROAD empowers robots to make informed decisions about critical road features, such as accident scenes and traffic rules. Our framework is tailored for robots operating in dynamic environments, where they must balance road safety protocols and human social norms. $\pi$-ROAD's modular design allows for seamless integration of various perception systems, such as LiDAR and computer vision, to detect road obstacles and accidents. Our framework is validated through comprehensive simulations and real-world experiments, showcasing its effectiveness in navigating complex road scenarios.

This paper presents a novel approach to creating a virtual model of a robot for the purpose of simulating its behavior in a collaborative environment. The model is designed to replicate the robot's movements and reactions to external stimuli, taking into account its inherent limitations and collision avoidance capabilities. By incorporating the Artificial Potential Fields algorithm, the virtual model is able to navigate around obstacles and interact with its surroundings in a realistic manner. Furthermore, the model is capable of adapting to changes in its environment, such as the movement of other robots, in a predictable and reliable way. The proposed model is then evaluated through a series of simulations, which demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately replicating the behavior of a real robot equipped with a depth camera.

The escalating presence of autonomy and machine intelligence will profoundly impact the physical and logistical layout of cities. As a result, urban planning will need to adapt to this transformation, with a pressing need to develop a clear vision for the future of cities. To address this, a novel approach is proposed, which combines a theoretical framework with a practical tool to facilitate a collaborative, multi-stakeholder process. The theoretical component is rooted in a conceptual model, while the practical aspect is a digital platform, and a case study of its application in the city of Berlin is presented.

In the context of online caching, we examine a scenario where a cache of fixed capacity is used to store items from an infinite library, with a random request sequence generated based on a known distribution. However, the online algorithm is unaware of this distribution, receiving only partial information about the requests in real-time. Our study focuses on the competitive ratio of caching algorithms, with a specific investigation of the Least Recently Used (LRU) strategy in various scenarios. The results show that the competitive ratio of LRU is directly related to the prediction error, cache size, and number of requests, with a specific upper bound that can be precisely calculated.

This paper presents a novel Trilateral Attention Network (TAN) for medical image segmentation, which integrates three distinct pathways to capture the spatial, scale, and intensity variations within images. By incorporating a novel spatial attention mechanism, TAN effectively isolates the most relevant image features. Additionally, TAN incorporates a scale and intensity attention mechanism to dynamically assess the relative importance of features across different scales and intensity levels. Our experimental results demonstrate that TAN achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, both in quantitative and qualitative assessments.

The superconnection $\mathcal{A}$ is derived from $e$ and $\bar{\varGamma}$, and its associated curvature is expressed as a function of the super gauge field $B$. The superconnection $\mathcal{A}$ is shown to be invariant under the torsion constraint, and the super gauge field $B$ is invariant under the condition that its associated curvature vanishes. This study introduces a novel approach to evaluating data reliability by pinpointing training examples that significantly impede model development. Our method enables the assessment of each training example's influence on model performance, ultimately allowing for the prioritization of reevaluation. We validate our approach by applying it to two datasets: a simulated dataset and a real-world dataset consisting of images from the MNIST handwritten digit recognition challenge.

In a quantum spin Hall system, we demonstrate that a non-abelian Berry phase can induce a Hall surface-based charge pump, which is unaffected by the system's underlying symmetry. This discovery reveals that the non-abelian Berry phase can be utilized as a tunable control to efficiently manipulate the Hall current in the surface state.

We introduce METRO-LM, a highly efficient and scalable language model that achieves comparable results to its larger counterparts while utilizing significantly less memory and computational power. This is made possible by METRO-LM's ability to process input data in parallel, utilizing a novel approach to partitioning and recombining data. This approach is paired with a specialized tokenization technique that maintains the integrity of the input's semantic meaning. Our evaluation of METRO-LM on various benchmarks reveals that it outperforms smaller models and is on par with the performance of its more substantial counterparts, all while being up to 10 times more memory-efficient and 3 times more computationally efficient.

Inferring the quantum network structure is crucial for various applications, but existing methods have limitations. They either require complete access to the network or rely on time-consuming global measurements. We introduce a new approach that infers the quantum network structure using only local measurements, but this time in an offline context. By analyzing the correlation patterns of local measurements, we can accurately infer the network topology. This method has practical applications, such as identifying the initial spread of quantum information and detecting network faults.

This paper presents a comprehensive guide to creating an interactive, web-based system for teaching visual storytelling through data visualization, specifically tailored for high school students and educators. The system, known as VizView, utilizes a Raspberry Pi and a 7-inch touchscreen display to deliver an immersive experience. We outline our design process, key features, and development process, detailing the system's hardware and software requirements. The system's effectiveness was evaluated through a pilot study, where we assessed its ability to engage students and facilitate learning. Notably, our findings suggest that an introductory video, followed by interactive exercises, is the most effective approach to teaching visual encoding. VizView's source code and design plans are freely available for public use, and we encourage replication and further innovation.

We investigate the impact of Floquet heating on quantum order in a Rydberg model, which is an extension of the Ising model. By simulating the impact of Floquet heating, we find that the quantum order in the Rydberg model is lost at a certain point, beyond which the system transitions into a chaotic state. Our research also reveals that the quantum order in the Rydberg model is resilient to certain types of disorder, which is a significant advantage for experiments.

In the context of model-based planning, we examine how to create effective counterfactual plans when the parameters of a model are subject to uncertainty. To address this challenge, we propose a method that uses a probabilistic approach to determine the optimal model parameters and then generates a set of robust counterfactual plans. Our evaluation of this method in a simulated environment demonstrates its ability to produce plans that are resilient to uncertainty and better suited to achieving our objectives.

This study introduces a novel approach to classifying audio from urban environments by combining a convolutional neural network with a pre-trained model that has been trained on a large dataset of natural images. The proposed method demonstrates high accuracy on two benchmark datasets, achieving an 64.4% and 63.6% error rate on the ESC-50 and US8k datasets, respectively, which surpasses the current state-of-the-art results. Furthermore, the method's ability to generalize to unseen sound classes is evaluated, and the model's weights are made publicly available for further research.

We investigate the thermodynamics of black holes in $N=4$ gauged supergravity, particularly focusing on a specific class of $AdS_4$ black holes. These black holes can be derived from a combination of $AdS_2 \times S^2$ and $AdS_2 \times H^2$ geometries, and their thermodynamic properties are explored using the first law of thermodynamics. The results show that the entropies of these black holes can be unified into a single expression, which applies to both cases. Additionally, we examine the phase transitions between these black holes and identify a specific transition point.

The SCAMP-5 benchmark, developed by the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, assesses the performance of spacecraft software in areas such as scheduling, communication, and fault tolerance. JPL's SCAMP system, used in spacecraft like the Mars 2020 Perseverance rover, is a sophisticated software stack that requires significant resources to execute. To evaluate Cain's ability to generate efficient code for this benchmark, we modified the JPL SCAMP-5 test suite and created a test harness. Our results indicate that Cain produces code that is 1.5 to 3 times shorter than that of other compilers, resulting in substantial reductions in binary size, memory usage, and execution time.

We investigate the generalized Witten effect in the context of a Schwarzschild black hole, drawing parallels with the behavior of a quantum harmonic oscillator in an external gauge field. By examining the spectrum of charged states, we derive a thermal spectrum that enables us to establish a connection between the generalized Witten effect and the emergence of Hawking radiation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the generalized Witten effect can be understood as a result of the quantum gravitational vacuum's response to the electric field, thereby providing a new perspective on the phenomenon.

Recent studies have demonstrated that a specific type of pruning can be used to learn 2-player Nash equilibria in polynomial time, and this method has been extended to multi-player games with a guarantee of convergence. However, this extension comes with a drawback, as it requires a significant amount of memory space that scales exponentially with the number of players. To address this limitation, this paper introduces two variations of the original regret pruning approach, which can be implemented efficiently even in large-scale games. The new variations are proven to have a guaranteed convergence rate, and they can be used to develop a more efficient algorithm for learning Nash equilibria in multi-player games.

This study presents a novel modal logic, drawing from Aristotle's modal syllogistic. This logic posits that possible states-of-affairs serve as the fundamental units of possibility and necessity. The resulting system is shown to be both sound and complete, and can be viewed as a dynamic extension of the standard modal logic, where accessible states-of-affair relationships mirror traditional world-accessibility relations. The logic is further illustrated through its application to the semantics of modal language and its use in deriving the principles of modal logic.

Causal structures can be defined using causal diagrams, which can be represented as directed graphs. Causal inequalities can be expressed as constraints on these diagrams, with the Bell inequalities being a specific type. In contrast to quantum systems, where perfect violation of Bell inequalities is achievable even with low detection efficiency, classical systems can still violate causal inequalities with low detection efficiency. However, it has been found that certain causal inequalities, such as the C-not and diamond inequalities, exhibit a significant reduction in their violation limit when detection efficiency is below 100%, whereas they remain unaffected by it at 100% efficiency. This result is attributed to the non-locality of quantum systems, which can be exploited to achieve high precision in device-independent tasks.

This paper introduces a dual-critic reinforcement learning framework for dynamic video encoding that addresses distortion and rate constraints simultaneously. Unlike conventional methods that employ a single neural network to estimate the reward, our proposed approach uses two separate networks to assess the degree to which the encoding constraints are met. By employing dual-critic networks, we are able to optimize the trade-off between the two constraints more effectively. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both rate-distortion performance and computational efficiency, achieving a 2.4-fold reduction in encoding time while maintaining comparable quality.

The chemical evolution of protoplanetary disks is significantly influenced by the interaction between the gas and dust components. In particular, the conversion of carbon-rich dust grains into gas through photo-ablation is a crucial process that can maintain a stable equilibrium in the disk's gas composition. This equilibrium is essential for the development of complex organic molecules in the disk's outer regions. In this study, we investigate the impact of this process on the development of complex organic molecules in the disk's outer regions. We find that the conversion of carbon-rich dust grains into gas can lead to a significant increase in the abundance of these molecules, particularly in the disk's outer regions. This increase in abundance is due to the enhanced availability of carbon and nitrogen in the gas phase, making it more conducive for the development of complex organic molecules.

Deep learning has been successfully applied to solving mixed-integer linear programming problems, with a focus on cut selection. This research introduces NeuralCut, a neural network-based model that learns from the behavior of branch-and-bound algorithms to make more accurate cut choices. Through extensive testing on the MIPLIB benchmark library, NeuralCut demonstrates a significant improvement in performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, with an average speedup of 1.4x and 1.2x on large-scale problems.

Our research focuses on the investigation of T$_d$-Mo$_{1-x}$Ir$_{x}$Te$_{2}$ single crystals, which exhibit a transition from a metallic to a superconducting state as Ir content increases. The superconducting properties of these crystals are characterized by a nodal gap, which is influenced by the presence of a specific type of crystal lattice distortion. The observed distortion is caused by the competition between electronic correlations and the crystal's structural anisotropy. The superconducting state in these crystals is further distinguished by a specific type of superconductivity, which is characterized by a nodal gap, and is likely the result of a novel type of electronic pairing.

A significant portion of software developers' time is spent searching for duplicate bug reports within bug tracking databases. Current methods for identifying duplicate bug reports rely on manual input, which is time-consuming and prone to errors. This paper introduces a novel approach that utilizes natural language processing techniques to automatically identify duplicate bug reports. The proposed method involves representing each bug report as a vector and utilizing a similarity threshold to determine if a report is a duplicate. The experiment's results, which utilized the Mozilla and Eclipse databases, demonstrated that the proposed method outperforms traditional methods, including the widely used "Cosine Plus" method.

A strongly coupled effective field theory for the critical Bose liquid phase of graphene has been developed, allowing us to study the phase transition from a pseudospin-1 Bose liquid to a pseudospin-1 Fermi liquid. This theory, grounded in the principles of the $J$-$\lambda$ transition in $^4$He, reveals that the critical exponent for the specific heat around the transition temperature is 1.

This study introduces a self-training teacher-student framework that enhances NER models by leveraging their capabilities. The proposed system is divided into two primary components: a teacher model and a student model. Initially, the teacher model is trained using a pre-existing NER model, and its predictions are utilized to annotate the training data, which is then used to train the student model. Subsequently, the student model replaces the original NER model, and this process is repeated iteratively. Through self-training, the NER model's performance improves, and this technique can be integrated into various NER models. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach on multiple benchmark datasets, and it achieves a significant performance gain, outperforming the state-of-the-art models by a considerable margin.

The tourism industry is a significant sector in the global economy, and understanding its dynamics is crucial for making informed decisions. Social media platforms like Instagram provide valuable resources, such as images and captions, that can be leveraged to extract insights. This study focuses on analyzing Instagram data from major tourist cities to identify patterns and trends in tourist behavior, and to offer recommendations to stakeholders in the travel and hospitality industry. By examining the geotagged data of popular tourist spots, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of how tourists interact with these locations and identify areas of interest. This information can be used to tailor marketing strategies, enhance customer experiences, and optimize resource allocation.

Predicting the effective properties of microstructured materials using machine learning algorithms has become increasingly efficient. However, these algorithms often fail to provide a clear physical interpretation of their results. To address this limitation, we have developed a novel machine learning approach that incorporates the physical properties of the material at the mesoscale. By leveraging this method, we can identify the optimal microstructure that maximizes a specific objective function. This approach was demonstrated through a case study involving a two-phase composite material with a rigid and isotropic matrix and a soft, isotropically elastic phase. The objective function was set to maximize the average stress in the soft phase. The resulting optimal microstructure was found to consist of isolated, spherical regions of the soft phase, surrounded by thin shells of the same material. The performance of the machine learning algorithm was validated by comparing its results to finite element simulations.

A recent study of the young star CI Tau and its planetary system revealed the innermost exoplanet, CI Tau b, to be migrating towards the star at a rate of 0.5 au per year. This phenomenon is thought to be caused by the interaction between the planet and the surrounding protoplanetary disk. However, a different explanation for the planet's movement is that it is actually a background object, such as a nearby star or planet, that was mistakenly identified as part of the system. To test this possibility, researchers used data from the SPHERE/IRDIS instrument at the VLT to see if they could detect a similar object in the same location. The results showed that the detection limits of the instrument were too high to rule out the possibility of a background object, but they were still able to set a useful limit on how far away such an object could be. This limit suggests that the background object, if it exists, would have to be at least 1000 au away from the star, which is consistent with the idea that the planet is actually a member of the system.

We demonstrate that the zero-energy trajectories in the Coulomb problem with a specified potential correspond to the high-energy paths of free motion on a large sphere. This is achieved by identifying the asymptotic properties of the Coulomb problem as energy approaches zero, thereby establishing a generalization of a previously known result. This new finding expands upon a previously established result, which itself was a generalization of a concept initially developed by Busemann.

This research investigates a class of non-local equations, which have a unique property that allows for a non-trivial solution, and leverages this property to analyze other related equations, such as the fractional Laplacian and the non-local double phase equation.

This paper introduces a novel solution to the data association problem in multi-object tracking, which is particularly effective in scenarios where no labels are available. By leveraging the concept of a random distribution over possible trajectories, the proposed method employs a single, unified latent variable to represent the state of all objects at a given time step. This approach allows for the efficient estimation of object trajectories and their corresponding associations, which is achieved through a computationally straightforward procedure. Furthermore, the proposed method eliminates the need for the data association process, thereby streamlining the filtering process. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in comparison to existing techniques, and show that it is well-suited for real-time applications.

This paper introduces a new stability assessment criterion grounded in the concept of
conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) to evaluate stability and security in power systems
with high penetration of power electronic interfaces. The proposed criterion is rooted
in the understanding that traditional stability assessment methods are inadequate for
complex systems featuring numerous control options. The CVaR metric quantifies
the expected losses associated with potential system instability and provides a
probabilistic measure of stability and security. The paper demonstrates the practical
application of the CVaR-based criterion through its use in stability analysis and
optimization of power control systems.

This study introduces a novel deep learning-based approach to developing automatic signature verification systems. The proposed method leverages a deep convolutional autoencoder to generate unique digital signatures for each user, as well as a forgery detection system that assesses the validity of a given signature. The efficacy of the forgery detection system heavily relies on the characteristics of the user signature template, including distinctiveness, complexity, and repeatability. The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional autoencoder to create a digital signature template for each user, which is then used to train a deep convolutional autoencoder to generate authentic digital signatures. The autoencoder is trained using a cross-entropy loss function, which is calculated based on the similarity between the generated signature and the user signature template. The proposed method also employs a deep convolutional autoencoder to detect forgeries, which is trained using a cross-entropy loss function, and evaluates the similarity between the generated signature and the user signature template. The proposed method is evaluated on the SIH2019 dataset, which contains 1,000 users, 1,000 genuine signatures, and 1,000 forgery signatures per user, and achieves a forgery detection accuracy of 99.5% and a genuine detection accuracy of 98.5%.

We establish Hardy sums as the generating functions for oriented geodesics, thereby developing a combinatorial interpretation of the Hardy prime number theorem. This is further extended to multigrade sequences, leading to a generalized Hardy prime number theorem applicable to multi-grading.

Mobile applications can offer a more tailored experience by leveraging contextual values that persist over time.  However, current approaches to persistent contextual values are limited in their ability to adapt to changing user behavior, and often fail to account for the complex relationships between different contextual elements.  To address this limitation, we propose a new framework for persistent contextual values that utilizes a probabilistic model to capture the dynamic relationships between different contextual elements.  This framework allows for the seamless integration of multiple contextual elements, and enables the identification of the most relevant contextual values at any given time.  We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a case study involving a mobile email client, and show that it can significantly improve the accuracy of contextual value predictions.

This research introduces a groundbreaking approach to pose estimation that achieves real-time performance without relying on deep neural networks. The proposed architecture leverages a combination of a convolutional neural network and a recurrent neural network to predict key pose indicators, while utilizing a fully connected network to refine the predictions. The system operates in real-time by processing frames sequentially, thereby enabling accurate pose estimation at 60 frames per second. The proposed method surpasses existing state-of-the-art pose estimation techniques in terms of accuracy, while also offering the unique advantage of being entirely model-free. The proposed system is also capable of generating 3D pose heatmaps from 2D keypoints, thereby facilitating the estimation of 3D poses. The proposed method is thoroughly evaluated using multiple datasets, including the Human3.6M, MPII, and VOT2018 datasets, and is shown to outperform existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy. The proposed method is also demonstrated to be highly effective in real-world applications, such as human action recognition, and is shown to outperform existing state-of-the-art techniques in this context. The proposed system is also shown to be highly robust to occlusions, thereby making it a highly effective tool for real-world applications.
